speaker: Kimi K3
text: ICICI Bank's 16% revenue growth and consistent EPS beats show the franchise is compounding at a 12% five-year CAGR, but at 4.2% off its all-time high the risk-reward is tighter than Union Bank's 35% five-year CAGR and 37.7% discount to its peak. For your Rs 10,000, ICICI buys only 7 shares versus 63 shares of Union Bank, so the dividend yield (1.64% vs 5.38%) and absolute rupee upside both favor the PSU play. On the US side, $100 in fractional NVDA at a 25% CAGR reaches roughly $125 in one year — still a long way from the $1,000 target without leverage or a multi-bagger pick.
